# Resources {.unnumbered}

Additional material to go deeper, ordered along the chapters of the module. Most items were first collected for the CDE Online Summer School 2021 and updated in 2023 and 2026.

## Key reading

- Lannen, A. (2019). [Inequality: What's in a word?](https://boris.unibe.ch/130698/) (S. Bieri and C. Bader, Eds.). CDE Policy Brief 14. Centre for Development and Environment, University of Bern. Sheds light on current inequality trends and discusses policies to reduce inequality within and between countries.

## Data

- [World Inequality Database (WID)](https://wid.world/): income and wealth data for most countries, with graphs and an [income comparator](https://wid.world/income-comparator/).
- [World Inequality Report 2022](https://wir2022.wid.world/) (Chancel, Piketty, Saez, Zucman et al.).

## Chapter 1: Inequality, what's in a word?

- UN DESA. [Concepts of inequality](https://www.un.org/en/development/desa/policy/wess/wess_dev_issues/dsp_policy_01.pdf). Development Issues No. 1. Outcome- and opportunity-oriented views.
- Stewart, F. (2016). [Changing perspectives on inequality and development](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12116-016-9222-x.pdf). *Studies in Comparative International Development* 51: 60 to 80.
- Michael Sandel: [Justice, Episode 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kBdfcR-8hEY). Overview of theories of justice from his Harvard lecture.
- INET: [Inequality 101](https://www.ineteconomics.org/perspectives/videos/inequality-101). Video series by Arjun Jayadev and Branko Milanovic.
- Ha-Joon Chang: *Inequality: What is it and why does it matter?* Lecture in the INET series [Economics for People](https://www.ineteconomics.org/perspectives/videos/economics-for-people) on what inequality is and how it is measured.

## Chapter 2: A tale of two stories

- Pitchfork Economics: [What is the trick in trickle down? (with Yuval Harari and Molly Crockett)](https://pitchforkeconomics.com/episode/what-is-the-trick-in-trickle-down/). Podcast.
- Finn Tarp and Miguel Niño-Zarazúa (UNU-WIDER): [Trends in global inequality](https://cepr.org/voxeu/video/trends-global-inequality). VoxEU video: relative global inequality has fallen, absolute inequality has risen.
- Gradín, C. (2024). [Revisiting the trends in global inequality](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.worlddev.2024.106607). *World Development* 179: 106607.

## Chapter 3: Why is inequality rising?

- Robert Reich: [Everything you need to know about the new economy](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fMmH_2EYohQ). Video.
- Thomas Piketty: [New thoughts on capital in the twenty-first century](https://hbr.org/video/embed/4102770682001). Harvard Business Review video.
- Lazonick, W. (2014). [Profits without prosperity](https://hbr.org/2014/09/profits-without-prosperity). *Harvard Business Review*.
- James Robinson: [Why nations fail](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=btMLcRC36m0) (TEDxAcademy). Talk on the role of institutions.
- Dabla-Norris, E. et al. (2015). [Causes and consequences of income inequality: A global perspective](https://www.imf.org/external/pubs/ft/sdn/2015/sdn1513.pdf). IMF Staff Discussion Note 15/13.
- Richard Wilkinson: [How economic inequality harms societies](https://www.ted.com/talks/richard_wilkinson). TED talk on inequality, health, life expectancy, and trust.

## Chapter 4: The way forward

- Mariana Mazzucato: [The market shaping forces of capitalism](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qSt5suImn78). Lecture introducing the Rethinking Capitalism course.
- Pitchfork Economics: [Why we need a mission-driven economy (with Mariana Mazzucato)](https://podcasts.apple.com/it/podcast/mission-economy-with-mariana-mazzucato/id1445901378?i=1000574743165). Podcast.
- Nick Hanauer: [The dirty secret of capitalism, and a new way forward](https://www.ted.com/talks/nick_hanauer_the_dirty_secret_of_capitalism_and_a_new_way_forward). TED talk on reciprocity and cooperation.
- Carlota Perez: *Technological revolutions and the shape of tomorrow*. Lecture; see her [list of recorded lectures](https://carlotaperez.org/videos-of-lectures-and-panels).
- Gough, I. (2020). [The case for universal basic services](https://doi.org/10.31389/lseppr.12). *LSE Public Policy Review* 1(2).
- Bader, C., Bieri, S. (2023). A world drifting apart: Challenges and possibilities of transitioning to a more equitable planet. In *Transitioning to Reduced Inequalities*. MDPI.
